question_en:
The small development board I have will no longer power on, and the text on the board surface is illegible, but I still want to reuse its enclosure and connector cutouts. Based on the attached images, please answer the following questions in order:

1. **Who is the manufacturer of this development board, and what is its specific model?**
2. **Within the same product family, which models meet the following appearance criteria?**  
   From the official product page of the identified model, navigate to the official family comparison page. For each model, use the first image on its product page (linked from this version of the comparison table) that meets the criteria: "white background, board only, component side facing up, connectors on the left." Then, item by item, determine: whether the shape of the connectors on the left end matches the attachment, whether the right half of the board has a major silver or light-colored shielding module, and whether a narrow antenna zone or keep-out zone extending to the right board edge is immediately adjacent to the outer side of the module. Please list the models that simultaneously satisfy these conditions.
3. **Among the models identified above as matching the appearance, which ones support Bluetooth LE but do not support Wi-Fi?**  
   Please verify against the "Bluetooth LE" and "Wi-Fi" rows in the same version of the comparison table, and provide the names of the models that ultimately meet the criteria.

Answer format: For Question 1, provide the manufacturer and model in text. For Questions 2 and 3, list the models matching the appearance criteria and the final qualifying models, respectively, in text.
answer:
Question 1: Manufacturer: Arduino; Model: Nano 33 BLE Sense Rev2.

Question 2: Nano 33 IoT; Nano 33 BLE; Nano 33 BLE Sense Rev2; Nano RP2040 Connect.

Question 3: Nano 33 BLE; Nano 33 BLE Sense Rev2.

# Detailed Simulated Retrieval Trajectory · 8-1-F01-1

## Step 01 · inspect_image / Establish identity clues using board structure

Action: Examine the current cropped image of the component side; record the two rows of gold-plated holes, connectors on the left end, buttons, sensor layout, and the outline of the module on the right.

Evidence observation (archived evidence summary): Multiple areas including the manufacturer, model, and module QR code are obscured by mosaics; cannot claim to have read the model printed on the board. Still visible are the slender board shape, the Micro-USB form factor on the left end, a light-colored square module in the right half, a narrow green board edge zone on its outer side, and a recognizable layout of small central components.

Result of this step: Use the structure and relative positions of components to find official product images; characters are not used as seed evidence.

## Step 02 · search + open_image / Recover Arduino Nano 33 BLE Sense Rev2

Action: Example query: "Arduino Nano Micro USB sensor board silver module right antenna"; match the official board image from the website point-by-point with the hole positions, round button, central sensor, and module boundaries in the attachment.

Evidence observation (archived evidence summary): The official component-side image of the Nano 33 BLE Sense Rev2 corresponds to the attachment; it shares a family outline similarity with the Nano 33 BLE without Sense, but differs in the number and layout of central sensors. The product title provides the manufacturer Arduino and the full Rev2 model; cannot use "BLE" printing for identification because that area is obscured.

Evidence links:
- Official product page: https://store.arduino.cc/products/nano-33-ble-sense-rev2
- Official image used for seed comparison: https://store.arduino.cc/cdn/shop/files/ABX00069_02.front_934x700.jpg?v=1727100949

Result of this step: Identify manufacturer as Arduino, model as Nano 33 BLE Sense Rev2.

## Step 03 · enumerate / Enter Nano family comparison table from product

Action: Follow the family information linked from the official product page to enter the Nano Family, and register all columns in the comparison table starting with Microcontroller.

Evidence observation (archived evidence summary): This version of the table has a total of 9 columns, starting from Arduino Nano and ending with Nano R4; in sequence: Arduino Nano; Nano ESP32; Nano 33 IoT; Nano 33 BLE; Nano 33 BLE Sense Rev2; Nano RP2040 Connect; Nano Every; Nano Matter; Nano R4. Pin headers, no pin headers, packaging, and combination kits for the same board type are not counted as separate models; new boards added in other periods are not appended to this version of the comparison scope.

Evidence links:
- Official family comparison page: https://store.arduino.cc/pages/nano-family

Result of this step: Fix the 9 basic board types; associate each model one-to-one with the table columns.

## Step 04 · select_images / Locate comparison images according to unified rules

Action: For the product pages linked in the 9 columns, search the image sequence to find the first image with a white background, board only, component side facing up, and connectors on the left.

Evidence observation (archived evidence summary): Do not mechanically take the first image from the product gallery: the first image might be an oblique view or include packaging. Source images have been recorded according to the rules of this question; the right half and right board edge in the images are always interpreted with the connectors on the left. The three appearance criteria are: consistent connectors, major shielding module, and a narrow antenna/keep-out zone immediately adjacent to the outer side of the module extending to the board edge.

Evidence links:
- Comparison table and product links: https://store.arduino.cc/pages/nano-family

Result of this step: Only if all three conditions are simultaneously satisfied is it recorded as a hit for Question 2; do not infer appearance from wireless chip models.

Evidence observation (archived evidence summary): The left end has a larger Mini-B form factor connector, which differs from the Micro-USB form factor in the attachment; the right half also lacks a major shielding module and an antenna or keep-out narrow zone close to the right board edge.
